entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 source 66529975427235712: position at J2016.0. Distance: Hunt & Reffert (2023), Improving the open cluster census. II. An all-sky cluster catalogue with Gaia DR3, A&A 673, A114; CDS J/A+A/673/A114, Table 3 (clusters), Melotte_22: dist50 134.84134308 pc, the distance of the Pleiades, of which Pleione is a member; its own parallax (McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson 2017 adopt 117.096 pc from Gaia DR1 or the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007) is less certain than the cluster's depth (half its members within 2.70 pc of the centre), and the Hipparcos-era parallaxes of the bright Pleiades are the ones the cluster's distance controversy showed biased (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/A+A/673/A114): 134.84134308 +/- 2.7 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 7.2414 +/- 0.1255 mas (same row, RUWE 1.30), 57.7 standard errors, is not used. Proper motion: Gaia DR3 (same row): 19.496, -47.650 mas/yr. Radial velocity from SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 66529975427235712 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none.

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 6.558 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17851: radius 5.695 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 94.567 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.602) and temperature; scaled from the paper's distance, 117.096 pc, to the cluster's, 134.84 pc: at a fixed temperature the radius grows with the distance, so 5.695 x 134.84/117.096 = 6.558 solar radii (luminosity 125.4); scaled from the paper's distance, 117.096 pc, to the cluster's, 134.84 pc: at a fixed temperature the radius grows with the distance, so 5.695 x 134.84/117.096 = 6.558 solar radii (luminosity 125.4) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 7548 +/- 2496 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17851: effective temperature 7548 +/- 2496 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.495).

entries.subject: Color
entries.finding: Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 230: HR 1180; VizieR III/202, through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #b7c4ff. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: HD 23862 is not in the library; gaia-xp: Gaia DR3 published no sampled BP/RP spectrum of it; pulkovo: HR 1180 is not in the catalogue; kiehling: HR 1180 is not among its 60 stars; burnashev: BS 1180 is not in part2; kharitonov: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 7,548 K and log g 3.82 (u1 0.303, u2 0.330): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. Gravity: log g 3.82 from 2001A&A...378..861C; the 3 published values span log g 3.346 to 4.5, across which the limb law changes by at most 2.3% of the centre brightness.
